recent_posts.title: Joomla 6.1 Beta 3 released for testing ahead of April stable launch
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.1 Beta 3 has been released for testing, marking the last release before the language freeze. The update includes accessibility improvements, workflow fixes, editor width/height bug fixes, and a 'What's new' tour for 6.1. The stable release is planned for April 14, 2026, with Release Candidate 1 due March 31. Extension developers are encouraged to test their extensions against this beta and report bugs at issues.joomla.org. No new features will be added at this stage; contributions for new functionality should target Joomla 6.2.

recent_posts.title: Joomla! 8 sprint
recent_posts.summary: The Joomla project has published its official feature list for Joomla 8, translating the previously defined product strategy into concrete development initiatives for the core CMS. The list has been reviewed and approved by the Production Department and covers items already in progress as well as those awaiting contributors. It is described as a living pipeline rather than a fixed roadmap, with priorities subject to change. The announcement calls on developers, testers, designers, documentation writers, and coordinators to get involved and help drive execution.

recent_posts.title: Joomla 6.1 beta 1 released with feature freeze
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.1 Beta 1 is now available for testing, marking the feature freeze milestone. Extension developers can test compatibility and report issues before the stable release planned for April 14, 2026. The beta includes contributions from 17 developers and focuses on ensuring production readiness through community testing. No new features will be added during the beta phase, with future functionality planned for Joomla 6.2 later in the year.

recent_posts.title: Wrapping up the Alpha phase
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.1 Alpha 3 is now available for testing, marking the final alpha release before the beta phase begins in February 2026. This release includes 25+ merged pull requests covering features like configurable media crop ratios, MFA controls for superusers, CLI commands for extension management, and various dependency updates. The stable release is scheduled for April 14, 2026. Extension developers are encouraged to test their extensions against this alpha version and report issues. Planned features for 6.1 include a graphical workflow editor, performance improvements for large sites, WCAG 2.2 AA compliance, and AI integration via MCP servers.

recent_posts.title: Joomla 6.1 alpha 2 released for testing
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.1 Alpha 2 is now available for testing, targeting developers to test extensions and users to explore new features. Key additions include a built-in POW captcha and nocache version option for webasset manager. The stable release is scheduled for April 14, 2026, with planned features including a graphical workflow editor, performance improvements for large sites, WCAG 2.2 AA compliance, and rate-limiting framework. Extension developers are encouraged to test their code and report bugs before the feature freeze in February 2026.

recent_posts.title: Test the Future of Joomla
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.1 Alpha 1 is now available for testing, marking the start of development for the next version. The alpha release aims to help developers test extensions and discover new features before the stable release planned for April 14, 2026. Key features include a graphical workflow editor, improved article list performance, and WCAG 2.2 AA compliance work. The release follows a structured timeline with multiple alpha, beta, and release candidate phases. Extension developers are encouraged to test compatibility, report bugs, and contribute to documentation.

recent_posts.title: Joomla 6.0 Beta 3 released with 37 new features ahead of October stable launch
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.0 Beta 3 has been released for testing, marking the final beta before the stable release planned for October 14, 2025. This version includes 37 new features such as child templates, advanced versioning, new date/datetime fields, batch tag removal, and media manager improvements. The release focuses on backward compatibility with a dedicated plugin, code cleanup, and dependency updates including TinyMCE 8.0.1. Extension developers are encouraged to test their code and report issues before the production release.

recent_posts.title: Joomla 6.0 Beta 2 released for testing with 35 new features
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 6.0 Beta 2 is now available for testing, featuring 35 new features including new date/datetime fields, batch tag removal, media thumbnails for all file types, and TinyMCE 8.0.1 integration. The release includes 227 merged pull requests from 26 contributors and focuses on code cleanup, dependency updates, and backward compatibility improvements. The final stable release is scheduled for October 14, 2025, with developers encouraged to test extensions and report bugs before the production launch.

recent_posts.title: Joomla! 5.4.0 Beta 2
recent_posts.summary: Joomla 5.4 Beta 2 is now available for testing, featuring automated core updates as the major new functionality. The release is in feature freeze with the stable version planned for October 14, 2025. Extension developers are encouraged to test their code and report issues before the final release.

top_posts.title: Joomla 5.2.0 Beta 1
top_posts.summary: The Joomla Project has announced Joomla 5.2 Beta 1, aimed at providing developers a platform to test their extensions and allowing users to explore new features. The final release is scheduled for October 15, 2024. This beta version is not suitable for production and highlights include layout changes for mail templates, SEO improvements, multi-language enhancements, and bug fixes. Developers and users are encouraged to contribute by testing and reporting issues.

top_posts.title: Your first glimpse at Joomla! 5.3.0 Alpha1
top_posts.summary: The Joomla! Project has released the first Alpha version of Joomla 5.3 for testing. This release is aimed at developers to test their extensions and users to explore new features. It is not suitable for production sites. The final Joomla 5.3 release is scheduled for 16th April 2025, with several alpha, beta, and release candidate milestones planned. Key new features include various code removals, refactoring, and support for PHP 8. Extension developers are encouraged to participate by testing and reporting bugs.
